definitions.explanation: Used to introduce a hypothetical situation for discussion or consideration.
Used to introduce a concessive condition, often followed by ても.

examples.japanese: {仮|かり}に{宝|たから}くじが{当|あ}たったら、{何|なに}を{買|か}う？
examples.english: Supposing you won the lottery, what would you buy?

examples.japanese: {仮|かり}にそれが{本当|ほんとう}だとしても、{信|しん}じられない。
examples.english: Even if that were true, I wouldn't believe it.

examples.japanese: {仮|かり}に{失敗|しっぱい}しても、{諦|あきら}めない。
examples.english: Even if I fail, I won't give up.

notes:
FORMATION:
{仮|かり} (temporary/provisional) + に (adverb particle)

GRAMMAR PATTERNS:
・{仮|かり}に〜たら - supposing ~
・{仮|かり}に〜としても - even assuming ~
・{仮|かり}に〜ても - even if ~

COLLOCATIONS:
・{仮|かり}に〜だとする - assuming that ~
・{仮|かり}に{言|い}えば - hypothetically speaking
・{仮|かり}にそうだとしても - even if that's the case

SIMILAR WORDS:
・もし - if (neutral)
・たとえ - even if (emphatic)
・{万|まん}が{一|いち} - if by any chance
